ABC: Trump says he will lead 'movement' to end mail-in voting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=032126_1&amount=25]
Be prepared to hear about this all the way through the midterms, Team .
President Donald Trump has said that he is leading a "movement" to get rid of mail-in ballots and voting machines , falsely claiming that they lead to voter fraud.
Word for lying word: " I am going to lead a movement to get rid of MAIL-IN BALLOTS, and also, while we're at it, Highly 'Inaccurate,' Very Expensive, and Seriously Controversial VOTING MACHINES, which cost Ten Times more than accurate and sophisticated Watermark Paper, which is faster, and leaves NO DOUBT, at the end of the evening, as to who WON, and who LOST, the Election. "
How is Trump going to do this? He's signed an executive order targeting November's critical midterms. Has this been just another attempt to distract from a failing economy, rising prices, and his role in the Epstein scandal? Probably, yes. Are we still fighting him tooth and nail? Definitely, yes.
We're working in the states to defend our access to cast ballots, as states run our elections. We're petitioning members of Congress to stop harmful bills that might attempt to back up this executive order. And we're going to do everything we can to support the efforts to stop this in court.
We'll be blunt: We still need your help to protect our fundamental right to vote. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to defend vote by mail across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=032126_1&amount=35]

Trump has long lied about mail-in voting. He's claimed mail-in voting contributed to his 2020 election loss, though no widespread fraud has been found. In fact, the one case of mail-in ballot fraud in Pennsylvania after the 2020 election was a man who was prosecuted for returning his dead mother's ballot for Trump .
We all know just how safe and secure mail-in voting is. It's use dates back to the Civil War. The use of mail-in voting has become very common across the country and study after study has shown that fraud in mail-ballot voting is rare. There are also several safeguards in place nationwide to protect against fraud, including signature requirements and barcodes to track envelopes sent by officials. States have spent tens of millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing.
Being blunt: There is no good-faith reason to limit vote-by-mail access. There is no good-faith reason to end the use of mail-in voting, or do the other things in this forthcoming executive order or his previous one attacking vote-by-mail. Just like the wave of redistricting efforts in Texas, Florida, and beyond -- this is a partisan voter suppression exercise meant to codify MAGA's power in perpetuity and end our democracy.
Opponents of voting rights will go to any length necessary to stop people from voting and stay in power. Help us fight back with $35 or whatever you can to protect mail-in voting and stop their suppressive policies >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=032126_1&amount=35]

name: Eric Metaxas
subject: Imagine this, it's horrifying.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Save the Persecuted Christians
body:
The threat is real. Persecution that starts overseas doesn't always stay there.

| | | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zifah929s3nrb4b5hcckei29s1gq2coj1kdeu0b8_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge0o74cjh2bs)
---
Dear Faithful Friend, **Imagine this:** A man steps outside his own home in a quiet neighborhood. Suddenly, violence erupts, his kneecap shattered in a brutal attack. His car torched. His family terrorized for years, children taunted with slurs in the streets, living under police protection for nearly a decade. This isn't a scene from some distant war zone. **This happened in Bradford, England – to Nissar Hussain.** **His only "crime"? Leaving Islam and embracing Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior.** For 17 years, Nissar endured relentless persecution from his former community. The Church of England? _**SILENT.**_ Not one bishop stood with him or his family. **But Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member, refused to stand by. We brought Nissar here to the U.S. to help him share his story, and he is now fighting back boldly – in part by pursuing a groundbreaking legal case against 11 countries that still mandate death for apostasy. ** [**Your support has amplified his voice and his mission to expose this evil.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2uqurffcrb379s6tvs4uq14g3mt8ns965e685m0_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge0o74cjh2bs) Nissar's story is heartbreaking, but it's not isolated. Over 380 million Christians face severe persecution globally, and the numbers are growing. _**In Iran, 254 believers were arrested**_ in 2025 alone for simply practicing their faith, escalating further amid the regime's war on Christians. _**In Nigeria, thousands have been slaughtered**_ by Islamist militants: entire villages massacred, girls held captive for years, all because they refused to deny Christ. _**In Pakistan, blasphemy laws **_are twisted to destroy Christian lives. _**In North Korea, owning a Bible**_ can mean a lifetime in a labor camp. **It is for all of these reasons that Save the Persecuted Christians is relentlessly educating Americans and rallying the faithful to recognize the threat before it takes deeper root here.** A powerful example: Our ongoing education and advocacy efforts helped fuel the overwhelming success on March 3, when **95% of Texas Republican primary voters stood up and voted to ban Sharia law** – sending a clear, faithful message: We will not let this ideology gain a foothold in America and threaten our freedoms or our persecuted brothers and sisters in Christ. **The threat is real.** _Persecution that starts overseas doesn't always stay there._ We must be extra vigilant, and **we need your help right now** to keep pushing back. [**Q1 ends at midnight on March 31, and we’ve set a goal of 1,000 individual donations from believers across America to sustain this vital work. Will you be one of them today?**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zv0ke5en0n7pt42hnjkukfho478e6eocce6vih8g_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge0o74cjh2bs)
---
[SAVE CHRISTIANS](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zfsgtomgga8fo5dntc8o5efjk47h58m29l9hork0_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge0o74cjh2bs)
---
Your gift, especially a monthly commitment through The Defenders Guild, multiplies our impact and sustains the fight against this growing evil. [**Click here to give and carry the burden with us.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zu82b1g599cipr24mk2nmet023vuases2t4ui4i8_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge0o74cjh2bs) [**From media campaigns to conferences and everything in between, I’ve seen firsthand how effectively and tirelessly Save the Persecuted Christians guides a coalition of 200+ leaders in order to expose evil and rally the Church – and any support you can offer is well-placed.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zsngbphjh9u3978ee22fem8o1pvkrriejjgcpe0g_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge0o74cjh2bs) **Paul wrote in Galatians 6:2, **_**“Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.”**_ **That is our mandate as the Body of Christ.** The Church must rise in one spirit, refusing silence in the face of darkness. Thank you for your faithfulness and courage in this hour. In Christ,
---
---
Eric Metaxas Member, Board of Directors Save the Persecuted Christians

A powerful example: Our ongoing education and advocacy efforts helped fuel the overwhelming success on March 3, when 95% of Texas Republican primary voters stood up and voted to ban Sharia law – sending a clear, faithful message: We will not let this ideology gain a foothold in America and threaten our freedoms or our persecuted brothers and sisters in Christ. The threat is real. Persecution that starts overseas doesn't always stay there. We must be extra vigilant, and we need your help right now to keep pushing back. Your gift, especially a monthly commitment through The Defenders Guild, multiplies our impact and sustains the fight against this growing evil. Paul wrote in Galatians 6:2, “Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.” That is our mandate as the Body of Christ. I've been around the block long enough to know one thing for certain: [You can trust the Democrats about as far as you can throw the dome off the Capitol.](https://trk.emails.stayinformednow._OA)
These high-fliers in D.C. think they know better than you do, and they'll look you right in the eye and tell you a bald-faced lie if it helps them keep their power.
They'll tell you dudes in dresses belong in girls' locker rooms... that illegals ain't voting in our elections... that thugs are just "justice-involved individuals"... and that trillion-dollar handouts ain't bankrupting your grandkids.

A Special Message from our SponsorPlease note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of Parler and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Parler.
Sound of FreedomA rescue team changed Kristen’s life. Another mission begins in Phoenix. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE

Friend,

No one could hear her.

A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic.

No windows. No fresh air. No way out.

The door was locked from the outside.

For months she lived there.
Alone.

There was no bathroom.
Just a bucket.

No shower. No clean clothes.

And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex.
Over. And over. And over.

This is the reality of child trafficking.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Send help to children waiting

Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world.

But Kristen’s story did not end in that attic.

One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another “date.”

But instead…she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers.

When Kristen realized she was safe…

She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates.

Free.

Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal.

She took the first step toward healing.

This rescue was possible because people chose to act.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Send help to children waiting

The Sound of Freedom Foundation exists to stop the sale of God’s children.

Inspired by the film Sound of Freedom, the Foundation works around the world to prevent trafficking, support rescue efforts, educate families, raise awareness, and push for stronger laws that protect children.

Our mission is simple.

To stop the sale of God’s children.

And right now we are preparing a new mission, happening in just a few weeks in Phoenix.

Our Freedom Strike Force partner will train local law enforcement for two days, teaching them how to identify traffickers and victims hidden in plain sight.

Then on day three…they go into the field.

Real operations. Real arrests. Real rescues.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

Children like Kristen are waiting.

But these missions cannot happen without support from people who care.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Send help to children waiting

That is why I am reaching out to you today.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Would you consider making your first gift of $30, $60, $130 or whatever you can do right now to help rescue children from trafficking?

Your donation today can help:

- Train officers to find trafficked children
- Support rescue operations
- Provide food, clothing, and care for survivors
- Help children begin the journey to healing

When I first heard the stories of trafficked children, I asked myself a question.

What if it were my child?

I could not stay silent.
And you do not have to either.

Friend, will you please help rescue the next child today?

Your gift — whatever God places on your heart — will help bring freedom to children still waiting in the dark.

Together we can make sure more children hear the Sound of Freedom.

With gratitude and prayer,

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D

Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For the Sound of Freedom Foundation

P.S. The cost to staff, equip, and execute a Freedom Strike ForceTraining Camp is $25,000. To raise these funds, I need Freedom Fighters like you to rally in support and sponsor this mission.

Please pray about what you can do to help and donate today.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D
Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation

name: AMAC Action
subject: We need to reach 1 million patriots calling for term limits
body:
You know it and I know it -- Congress is broken.

| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zk3175cb1lafq08d5b31kqrt6r5lf2135a2a8vu0_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)
---
| | Dear Fellow Conservative,You know it and I know it -- Congress is broken. Politicians have turned “serving the people” into “serving themselves.” They use their positions to get richer and richer every year, while you and I get left behind.Left-wing radicals like Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez work to destroy our country from within. And Washington never fixes anything. **[Today, WE THE PEOPLE have a chance to do something about it when you sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zi3jtga4hn3k9jj5j497qjcq6fi9a2ndhk0dsnk8_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)** Our Founding Fathers never intended for government service to be a permanent career. George Washington famously served just two terms — then went home.Our Founding Fathers also said our government was made for a “moral and religious people.” And they understood that if that moral compass broke down, Congress could easily steer America in the wrong direction, become a do-nothing body, or make government a gravy train for themselves.That’s why they included a powerful safeguard in our Constitution -- an escape hatch -- enshrined in Article V. If Congress ever became too corrupt to fix itself, Article V. says the states can use this provision in the Constitution to act.34 state legislatures can call a convention, propose term limits -- and Congress can’t do a thing about it. [**Here at AMAC Action, we have led the term limits movement in the past, and we are ready to put our efforts behind the movement once again.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z0agf54ec9iojag2uvblkpbpv27rnbk1tdjel9o8_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)
---
[ **Time for Term Limits** ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zpue4dgtkg6cubvcihcu33b8l2pio9d8pa1mv8q0_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)
---
My friend, can you imagine Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez spending 30 more years in Congress?? We are AMAC Action. “AMAC” stands for Association of Mature American Citizens. And when it comes to standing up for the rights of Americans, “action” is what we’re known for.President Trump has said that AMAC Action is so effective that members of Congress run the other way when they see our delegates coming down the hall. And our **“Time for Term Limits”** Petition Drive certainly has Washington lifers on the run![**Please sign your petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2oufi3rv39gqrnp6oah30tuclfleitl45lka3gg_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)
---
**>>** No more golden pensions for people who work 170 days a year and spend half of that just trying to get reelected.**>>** No more using the power of the office to destroy American values from within.**>>** No more insider deals to get rich.**>>** No more jobs for life with nothing to show for it!
---
Some of these grifters and America-haters have been “working” in Congress over 30, and even 40 years!
---
* **Maxine Waters — 34 years**
* **Chuck Schumer — 44 years**
* **Patty Murray — 33 years**

---
They’ve been in the swamp so long they’ve grown gills. Please – let’s not let them drag America down into the swamp with them. It’s time to use the escape hatch our Founders left for us.34 state legislatures are needed. What will embolden states to act is seeing a massive groundswell of support for term limits from millions of Americans just like you.That’s why AMAC Action is spearheading this massive 50-state Petition Drive and why you got my email today.You’ve proven that you’re a patriot who can be counted on to take action. **[Please sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours with your sacrificial donation of $35, $50 or more to spread this national campaign across America.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z0g6tn820slel55mecujn87giq4subqgu2h25l4o_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)** We need to reach **1 million** patriots with petitions just like yours.And that takes time and money.The Washington lifers are counting on having more power, influence, and resources than the American people.They’re counting on our complacency and despair.But here at AMAC Action we say: Let’s finish the fight our Founders began and restore America’s government to the people.Your $35 gift is enough to send and collect 50 more **“Time for Term Limits”** petitions across email, text, and mail. Your gift of $70 funds 100 more **“Time for Term Limits”** petitions.Singlehandedly, you are an indispensable force-multiplier in this effort. But if you do nothing, nothing changes.
---
* Immigration policy will never get fixed and just stay a meaningless election year talking point.
* America’s spending and debt will continue to grow unchecked. Remember when we had a balanced budget? We can get back there if career politicians do something!
* Social Security will keep getting raided while real policies to protect your benefits sit on the back burner.
* Healthcare costs will do nothing but skyrocket leaving seniors vulnerable.
* America’s children will stay trapped in the leftwing indoctrination centers we call “public schools.”
* Radicals like Ilhan Omar, Corey Booker, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez will continue to undermine America’s founding values.
* And the Washington, D.C. fat-cats will just get fatter and lazier.

---
Please join our army of patriots who are fed-up with the Washington lifers who work against our interests while our country sinks. What’s even more frustrating is that President Trump has policies that can save the ship and Washington lifers stand in his way! **[Your signed “Time for Term Limits” petition is critical. And we appreciate your donation whether it’s $35, $50 or anything higher or lower. What’s most important is that you respond in the next 72 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zakh0eabalqlk0231kgcpdbl2jmk0adhfvj70lno_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)** **One million “Time for Term Limits” petitions is a bold goal but we can do it if we all pitch in.** Every dollar helps. Every signature counts. Every day matters.Thank you and may God bless you and these United States.
---
| | With hope and urgency,
---
**Rebecca Weber,_Chairwoman_****AMAC Action**
---

Our Founding Fathers left us a Constitutional escape hatch in case Congress was sinking the ship. It’s Article V. of the Constitution and it’s time we use it to make term limits law. **[Please sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it with your emergency gift of $35, $50 or more in the next 72 hours.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zkvlmm8keko5fe12sdamft86tlgof0puj51kff60_rp22sh2s8i6epr1chge1o32c9h2bs)**

**Whatever happened to _CHiPs_?** _CHiPs_ arrived in 1977 at just the right moment for television. Airing on NBC, the show followed two California Highway Patrol officers, Ponch and Jon, as they cruised sunlit freeways on motorcycles. [Watch the theme song here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAUheGngS0WXDCkA0OlKFu6dkSALzEVDpG5sZW3r9xX6HqO9A3_983fQqnlcf8KCzrKzT9w7xWJcPVL6xRybusUYsVXT4UK9hZmDwLMSagTgJ9CqW-v-eQyIqDi6KS1WlotwfDZiYjCAiiINiUrxxTOZkQZPzKaYLXhxR2aUABSiLMehxQwmmjOwlitQCHTAqdCbR1-WnnQjLm-24brkNrCq5uJnp2pTwZXBtd934d3e9Er4vEfS6A0M3XdmLpcxlO8KAvb2Pnqpudeai3dWKbFfQml_pH0rw6bg98AAAD__9AXcE4). It blended action, humor, and a relaxed, family-friendly tone that stood apart from grittier cop dramas of the era. Audiences tuned in for spectacular crashes and stayed for the easy chemistry between Erik Estrada's charming Ponch and Larry Wilcox's steady Jon Baker. By the late 1970s, Estrada had become a full-fledged pop culture star. But the same partnership that powered the show also helped undo it. Behind the scenes, Estrada and Wilcox clashed over salaries, status, and personality differences. Tensions grew as the series wore on. Wilcox left after the fifth season in 1982, removing half of the show's central dynamic. Ratings slipped, budgets tightened, and NBC canceled _CHiPs_ in 1983. In syndication, however, the series found a long afterlife, cementing its place as a nostalgic staple of late-1970s television. A 1999 reunion movie brought [Estrada and Wilcox back together for longtime fans](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGngc3RcTYGBg9d2NK1IzLmiK8yGOFrUN6-Sl-h8y99w_91n-6eE--PT7-RkzVPO10lkQid05aL-HXN5-LnRD8lsDCV7OOEgFaBVojT4jm9JlMvbiVC0jW5putM05kGbR1d0GjbYHU_6B5xHoYZAs62hRC0D3ap2b010IgNQG_aW_A029n2YDujUVNlgBaWfN6-M-8SaU2v_KTzFvJWJxdFjlLpjwrHCseD8pHonSocr0gnKS5KIqkQ-Sgq-CJqz5dqmgEB2q4-3XJcnBIX21UGHpvn9EfLv348Hf4GAAD__0uXcys), but a 2017 big-screen comedy reboot with a new cast failed to capture the original's tone or audience. Estrada's career cooled after the show but never disappeared. He found renewed fame in Spanish-language television and later leaned into his on-screen persona by becoming a real-life reserve police officer. He remains active on the convention circuit and in occasional roles. Wilcox took a different path, stepping away from acting to pursue business ventures, and later facing legal trouble tied to a securities fraud case. Today, he lives largely out of the spotlight. Decades later, [the two men have reconciled](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6yAUgOGnwVssfMCYDAxXV3KXpkuHdkNgDvGpsImAxsrbV-krdP_1Df_HxV4cJdqvb25D02K2Ox41YWtY7JZrczHmEpxP-F0XaoQ1u9UCB3Xi4gRgg6P0sLILJiICig7NME1ymOQAqlvNKM8etR5HseDiueSSu8F7oc5-0jqKjsxT4wJg4FzLsV8ceuWV5mqSAgQyyTFQy6X_yrS3FWN65DuWfslbl8za2q0y8Y_BzGA-jqOnvTZ3LW57FgzmG4P5_yOk95fz66dFBnNXTLgdlBJVNTHJr5uj9Ou1P024G_gJAAD__4bGb4I), much like their characters once did, leaving behind a show remembered for its sunshine, sirens, and a partnership that defined its time. _Were you a fan of CHiPs? Airing on NBC, the show followed two California Highway Patrol officers, Ponch and Jon, as they cruised sunlit freeways on motorcycles. . It blended action, humor, and a relaxed, family-friendly tone that stood apart from grittier cop dramas of the era. Audiences tuned in for spectacular crashes and stayed for the easy chemistry between Erik Estrada's charming Ponch and Larry Wilcox's steady Jon Baker. By the late 1970s, Estrada had become a full-fledged pop culture star. But the same partnership that powered the show also helped undo it. Behind the scenes, Estrada and Wilcox clashed over salaries, status, and personality differences. Tensions grew as the series wore on. Wilcox left after the fifth season in 1982, removing half of the show's central dynamic. Ratings slipped, budgets tightened, and NBC canceled CHiPs in 1983. In syndication, however, the series found a long afterlife, cementing its place as a nostalgic staple of late-1970s television. A 1999 reunion movie brought , but a 2017 big-screen comedy reboot with a new cast failed to capture the original's tone or audience. Estrada's career cooled after the show but never disappeared. He found renewed fame in Spanish-language television and later leaned into his on-screen persona by becoming a real-life reserve police officer. He remains active on the convention circuit and in occasional roles. Wilcox took a different path, stepping away from acting to pursue business ventures, and later facing legal trouble tied to a securities fraud case. Today, he lives largely out of the spotlight. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

## Judge Blocks Islamic Development Efforts
A Collin [County judge issued a temporary restraining order](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ygzAQhJ8GOjGS-JEpVKShc9qUzIEOfBkheaQzmLfP4FdIt8Xuzu73cx_vQJ7C-g0bWn4vcQx4ZI_MmEZHOeCZj4PI4wrzCQE8bHEZtdSdkLXQenRA_hyb0tlJul6VaJUxjTJGd6p82E5rrPtp7pZZGdMaXDoF0NbtTTupmqkke5XJWmulpGxvFahGYm8W6J1TU9sXjURHHFPFD2R8Q178GXdM1Ry30tsH8zMX9Vehh0IPx3FUS3w3143LUOjhkoUePlHx-3IrCsr5hVkkzJyAAoVVxOQwCViBQmbxYvLEp3CUOdHMgsIe_Y5OUPaw0Swc7ujjc8PAZbLueZD3lDtTNHLdgPxnHf-P6W71XwAAAP__YYmQkQ) blocking a municipal utility district tied to the planned Islamic development, The Meadow, and halting operations ahead of a scheduled board meeting. State officials allege board members acted improperly to expand the district and [bypass regulatory oversight](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OhCAQgJ8GOwyM-FdQXGO3115pRhldsigG2GW9p7-4r3DlJF--mW9-buMNrbP7-o0b6fRe_LhTjo5SojAaG3c6Y87WOlpxPnFHh5tfRhDQcFFxgNGgdeeoCqMnYXpZkJZtq2TbQiOLu6ZmkWSgbohmmIWoatV3LZKaRNepGQurL5moAKQUou5KlEpQ3y7YGyOnumdKkLHJhzLdKdEb4-JO_6JQzn4rnL6ndERWfTEYGAw55_KCwgN3XPH3KrlABsNVxmC41jEYNgyfgcHwkfLZP0PiibbDBwzWnXxyfn5ETsviQ4o8eR6fx-FDYjAUQZsjW-dsbFqmxLqhdZ-L0v_--NLwFwAA__9oOYk2) for the project, which includes housing, a mosque, and a faith-based school. The developer disputes the claims and says the process followed standard procedures. [The restraining order](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO2zAQRU9DdTTIsSyuChZp1G3alMKYHNqTHYmGOLZWtw-cK2z9gY_33p_P-RNZeL39xoWifpc6r7Q3IVXa5sxtpaPtO7PQDdOBKwoutczgYLDubAHmjCzH3Hc5Xl0efUfRh9D7EGDw3T3CpVByCJeRSoGPIeQhOBgwFI9jonPH8X3mzgDeO3f5OKHvHY2h4Jizv15G0zvKrHU76Z2UvrEVOeqLtlOqSyfxrvpo5vzLwGRg2vf9hM-M6XjPBqavTbKB6a1lYJKaUAxMf5_5RvYqNX01-1QW1sNmbrpxUqtM2Wq1y7MJLzbTi6Q-Flq122J-7CzCbQimd7cFWf6D6M_yvSL8CwAA__9gQ4eL) prevents the district from taking most actions while the case proceeds, with a court hearing scheduled later this month to determine whether a longer injunction will be issued.
## Disney's WWII Legacy on Display in Dallas
A new exhibition at the [Dallas Holocaust and Human Rights Museum](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO3SAURVeDOyx49jdDQZHG3aRNaWF42E_C8AVksHcfTZQdpL7S1Tnn1-f2aSlSOn7aC027Q94S9hqxNSybp5rwqb0TRTyse2yy0V45bCBg4WLiAJu3FJ9tHrzZhddyQCOVmqVSsMjhNBgAQTnrJyfcKwSBuIgPqbTQTji1DGS-z8QEIKUQr4_RylmgVsFq7-X-0mwW6KnlMrYTG962hvjkLyyjy9cQzdnau7LpB4OVwdp7H9PufOjfM4MVU8PSLKULU2OwthN5dZiQwZqwc7xP2qlRThzvd8wFK_8nzkuOyP3vQungPZfoebeFEzFYJ631JIHBOhTj351ipLooNovjshT_srX_K_pl4E8AAAD__5aPjRU) explores how Walt Disney and his studio supported the U.S. war effort after Pearl Harbor, when the military occupied Disney's Burbank lot. Disney Studios devoted roughly 90% of its output to wartime production, creating training films, propaganda pieces, and over 1,200 military insignias using iconic characters like Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck. [The exhibition](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykzzFuwyAUANDT4C3W5wcbe2Do4i1dO6Kf8LGRsIkAhfj2Vdsj9AJPel83e6MQw7F-0s6mvn2yB7cSuVbO1oVy8FlaCyHySo-TDoq0J28RcLzA9YJoHYV4WtU5cwc3y46N1FpJrXGU3WZGT0q66T6wQucfHqZBjoAzeB5ZDVMXzA8GV0QpAYapJ6mAZ-1pdk7eh1koYBdqyn3duPKbio9nenHuH2nvotlqfRZx_RC4CFxaa73btrz3Ka8Cl7-DwKXLxj1biDGUUQsF604h_hL1f_GXwe8AAAD__2IkbNY) also highlights workforce shifts during the war, including women stepping into animation roles and the experiences of Japanese American employees, offering a broader look at how the studio adapted while contributing to the Allied effort. The exhibit runs through September and features more than 500 artifacts, films, and original artwork.
## Intact Alamo Cannonball Unearthed
Archaeologists at the Alamo uncovered a [fully intact bronze cannonball](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGuszAQBODTQEe0NhBD4eJv0uVvX4kWvIaVFhPhVQi3fwpXeP3MJ838PIcnsnCa_-NKXj9xGxIdWUiV9iFwTnTm42AWmnE6MaHgusXBgr1XUFfWDgFZzqEpgx8h9KYkb5xrjHP2bsrFB5hCR53FHsbaAMTYmXaaQgvBxbEdS_ZfDGprjQFouxuaBqh3EfsQzNj2RQMUWLf9pgspfTBHObc37bdpW0vxi-orF_W_wj4K-0ARXVAzJ6WdsnKav7nCPq5qdQ2oJkxpSyOKlLsPr4NFON9d0cC8Issl69_-eHv7GwAA__-u6Xck) dating to the 1836 battle, announcing the rare find just after the site's 190th anniversary. Researchers believe the [four-pound projectile](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCngc7INv7jULi4hi7XXokWe4GVFjvCeyG8_Sl5hetHo_nmz2N6ADHl9TfsGOS9lCnjWRlF8JgS1YxXPU8ixhXiBRkY9rJMVtub0r2ydkpAfE2uTWHWaTAtBuO9M97bm2m34GYPXi-9AUgxDfMQnb7rezTGJYfatBQ-Zbq31hitf-4dGKdx8AsMKZn5Z2icxkRSjk42FHxDXfgqLzy6WPaWwybyrE3_q7FjY8fzPLulvD38rUL5E2ns-DE1diS1wQtV3Ii5KjjiBli4rFSlqoVyUpQFoqgZRBjVF6si5FzyDMztEdLzJGaqN984ve5A_F0h__fdK9h_AQAA___1boam), discovered three feet underground, was likely fired by the Mexican Army, which primarily used bronze munitions. Experts are analyzing the cannonball to better understand its trajectory and role in the battle. The National Historic Landmark is undergoing a $550 million preservation project, and the discovery adds to a growing collection of combat relics from the historic conflict.

name: Grassroots Army
subject: We just hit #1 again…
body:
We just hit #1 again... and the mission is getting bigger
=======================================================

Click the image to watch 👇
==========================

You can buy the book here 👇
===========================

I had to send this email because the momentum keeps building... and I want you to hear this directly from me.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Men Are Forged, Not Found just hit #1 in Christian Leadership
-------------------------------------------------------------

and #1 in Religious Leadership on Amazon.
-----------------------------------------

Not in a month.
----------------

Not in a week.
---------------

In the first days.
-------------------

And I’ll be honest... I’m humbled by it.
--------------------------------------

Not because of the ranking itself —
------------------------------------

but because every single sale means someone out there wants change.
-------------------------------------------------------------------

A father buying it for his son.
-------------------------------

A wife buying it for her husband.
---------------------------------

A man buying it because he knows he’s capable of more.
------------------------------------------------------

That’s what this book was written for.
---------------------------------------

This isn’t about hype.
-----------------------

This isn’t about politics.
---------------------------

This isn’t about me.
---------------------

This is about the forge.
------------------------

It’s about discipline when you don’t feel like it.
---------------------------------------------------

It’s about responsibility when it’s hard.
------------------------------------------

It’s about faith when life tests you.
-------------------------------------

It’s about becoming the man you were meant to be.

In a press conference aimed at deflecting from the failure of Trump's Iran operation, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth stated "This was never meant to be a fair fight, and it is not a fair fight. We are punching them while they're down."
As you've seen by the rising price of crude oil skyrocketing to $120/barrel and the real concern that gas could cost up to $5/gallon, this does not appear to be the case. They are hitting us just as hard as we're hitting them.
And while Pete's metaphor was a fabrication Democrats on the other hand have an actual opportunity for an unfair fight where we can punch someone while they're down:

This is an all-hands-on-deck moment
|
---

Peter,
The Voting Rights Act of 1965 (VRA) is the crown jewel of the civil rights movement and the most effective law in our history at protecting the right to vote.
But right now, the VRA is facing an unprecedented assault by anti-democracy forces working to push our nation backwards. And some of these attacks are coming from the highest level — the Supreme Court.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127818488/609328461/-1482690219?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_SupCourtDeepDive_email_20260322-AOTL-Tier1-SupCourtDeepDive_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260322-AOTL-Tier1-SupCourtDeepDive_&utm_campaign=SupCourtDeepDive&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjU3ZDZhN2IxLWYwMjUtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=SdHJ7qcyG0U0kmuKRJorHfPVY5amkn2EvSEXgXXZ0fg=)
---
Under Chief Justice John Roberts, the Court is building a legacy that threatens the very foundations of our democracy. Here’s a quick recap of this shameful record so far:
_**Shelby County **_
In 2013, the Supreme Court’s _Shelby County_ ruling gutted Section 5 of the VRA, which mandated that states with a history of racial discrimination receive preclearance before enacting new election laws. Just moments following the decision, gerrymandered legislatures started passing a surge of voter suppression laws.
_**Malliotakis v. Williams**_
Earlier this month, the Supreme Court overturned a state trial court’s ruling requiring a Staten Island-based district to be redrawn for discriminating against Black and Latino voters. Justice Alito’s opinion concurring with the majority argued that VRA-compliant districts are no less racist than the racism they were created to address.
Justice Sotomayor gave a scathing dissent: “Time and again, this Court has said that federal courts should not interfere with state-court litigation. Time and again, this Court has said that federal courts should not meddle with state election laws ahead of an election. Today, the Court says: except for this one, except for this one, and except for this one.”
_**Louisiana v. Callais**_
These decisions have all led us to a decisive moment in the _Callais_ case. Any day now, the Court will issue a decision that could dramatically weaken Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, greenlighting discrimination and stripping citizens of the right to pursue legal action against gerrymandered districts.
[**We’re preparing to leap into action no matter the ruling, and we'll need unprecedented resources to defend our democracy against escalating attacks. This is an urgent moment that requires all of us — make a donation today to help us fight for fair maps and free elections.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127818490/609328464/-1482690219?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_SupCourtDeepDive_email_20260322-AOTL-Tier1-SupCourtDeepDive_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260322-AOTL-Tier1-SupCourtDeepDive_&utm_campaign=SupCourtDeepDive&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjU3ZDZhN2IxLWYwMjUtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=SdHJ7qcyG0U0kmuKRJorHfPVY5amkn2EvSEXgXXZ0fg=)

Large sporting events create the perfect conditions traffickers exploit. Packed hotels. Busy streets. Strangers coming and going. All of it creates cover for those who want to hide evil in plain sight. That is why the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists. We are a faith-driven movement dedicated to one mission:
**Stop the sale of God 's children.** Through prevention, education, and support for rescue efforts, we work to protect vulnerable children and help communities fight trafficking. Awareness was only the beginning. **The real mission was protecting children in the real world.** **Real lives were still at risk. **

But this year, something powerful happened **before the tournament even began.** Volunteers across Dayton stepped forward. **Ordinary people. Parents. Students. Believers.**
**People who refuse to look away. ** They gathered for a special training organized by partners of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation.** They learned how to recognize the warning signs of trafficking. They prepared outreach kits that included soap bars and makeup remover wipes with a hotline number that victims can call for help.

name: James Talarico for Senate
subject: Extremely underwater
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Talarico for Texas
body:
#
Peter —
Two polls in a row have shown James leading both Ken Paxton and John Cornyn.
But when we say it doesn’t matter who Republicans nominate, it’s not just about the head-to-head polling.
Let’s break it down.
John Cornyn has struggled to make it even this far. He’s the first U.S. Senator to face a runoff in decades in Texas. He basically tied Ken Paxton in the primary, despite more than $70 million in establishment spending on his behalf.

For years I've been the town crier in Tennessee warning against making the same cultural and legislative mistakes of my former home states of Washington and California. In a few instances I must give credit where it is due when those blue states get it right and my new home state gets it wrong. [California's Prop 13](https://substack.com/redirect/319cbf47-91d5-49f9-8114-6880385e96bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) real estate property tax cap is my best example. Tennessee is still one of only 5 states that don't have a cap and sure enough their counties hike on a whim.
As [Nashville Electric Service](https://substack.com/redirect/53bd6f0e-a04d-4f52-ba01-b626b9901429?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (NES) struggles to restore power to thousands of residents following Winter Storm Fern, the contrast between their emergency response and that demonstrated by [Puget Sound Energy](https://substack.com/redirect/74f89d0c-1098-4d41-b677-f694d7c202a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (PSE) during past extreme weather events highlights fundamental differences in utility readiness, communication strategies, and infrastructure investments. The current Nashville crisis reveals systemic failures that PSE has spent years addressing through strategic planning and technological innovation.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.718j_Cg8Mjn0t213L3etzfnJNNArv3ozE8wmhnDET0M?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=191767187)
PSE has consistently demonstrated superior restoration capabilities during severe weather events. When faced with Pacific Northwest storms that brought similar ice accumulation and wind damage to what Nashville is experiencing, PSE typically restored power to 80-90% of affected customers within 48-72 hours. By contrast, Nashville is reporting that tens of thousands of customers remained without electricity nearly a week after the ice storm, with officials warning that complete restoration could extend well into the following week.
PSE's strategic advantage lies in their pre-storm preparation protocols. Rather than merely reacting to weather events, PSE implements comprehensive readiness procedures when severe conditions are forecasted. Their crews are staged strategically across service areas, with equipment prepositioned where damage is predicted to be most severe. They maintain mutual aid agreements through coordinated networks across multiple states, ensuring additional resources can be deployed rapidly when needed.
According to reports from Tennessee's state leadership, Governor Bill Lee expressed concern that "Tennesseans need a clear timeline for power restoration, transparency on the number of linemen deployed, and a better understanding of when work will be completed in their neighborhood." This criticism highlights fundamental shortcomings in NES's response that PSE has addressed through their established protocols.
Perhaps the starkest difference between PSE's past performance and NES's current response lies in their communication with customers. During Nashville's ongoing crisis, tens of thousands of residents received incorrectly automated text messages alerting them that their power had been restored when they remained in darkness--a technical failure that created additional anxiety and confusion.
PSE has invested significantly in communication infrastructure that includes real-time outage maps, estimated restoration times by zip code, regular social media updates, and text alert systems with proven accuracy. Their outage management system allows customers to report outages through multiple channels and receive timely updates specific to their locations. The company maintains transparency about restoration priorities, explaining clearly that critical services like hospitals and emergency stations receive attention first, then areas with the largest affected populations, before moving to smaller outages.
Nashville officials appear to have struggled with communication transparency throughout this event, with Mayor Freddie O'Connell initially calling NES's leadership response "successful" before later changing course to state he was "not satisfied" with restoration efforts. This wavering confidence further eroded public trust in an already strained situation.
The foundation of PSE's superior performance lies in their long-term infrastructure investments. According to their reliability reports, PSE has systematically modernized their grid with underground lines in vulnerable corridors, equipment hardened against ice accumulation, and smart grid technologies that allow for faster outage identification and isolation. Their Seattle service area reports that "for the 20th consecutive year, service reliability experienced by [Seattle] customers was well above that experienced by all PSE customers in the aggregate."
PSE has embraced cutting-edge technologies to enhance their response capabilities. They've implemented advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to predict vulnerable infrastructure areas before storms hit. Their grid modernization includes real-time monitoring systems that automatically detect outages without customer reports, allowing for immediate dispatch of repair crews. Most notably, PSE has invested in Splunk's integrated monitoring platform which has "improved customer experience during power outages" and provided maintenance teams with unprecedented visibility into facility data.
The contrast with Nashville's situation is telling. Reports indicate that NES faced 444 broken poles during the ice storm, with only 107 fixed by the fourth day of restoration efforts. While the volume is certainly substantial, the slow progress suggests insufficient workforce allocation and potentially inadequate infrastructure hardening for known weather vulnerabilities.
PSE's workforce planning demonstrates superior strategic thinking. They maintain robust training programs that ensure crews are prepared for extreme weather conditions, with certification standards that exceed state requirements. Their mutual aid agreements through regional partnerships allow for rapid scaling of workforce when damage exceeds local capacity.
Reports from Nashville suggest that while NES ultimately deployed more than 1,000 lineworkers, this ramp-up appeared to happen after the crisis had already escalated, rather than as a precautionary measure. The delayed response extended outage durations and amplified community frustration.
The institutional culture at PSE emphasizes proactive crisis management rather than reactive problem-solving. Their leadership has established clear protocols for decision-making during emergencies, with designated spokespeople trained in crisis communication. By contrast, Nashville's crisis has featured shifting narratives from officials, with the Governor's office requiring direct intervention to demand transparency from NES.
The company's reliability reporting demonstrates their commitment to data-driven continuous improvement. PSE regularly publishes detailed performance metrics including System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) and System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) figures. This transparency builds public trust and holds leadership accountable for maintaining service standards.
The difference between Puget Sound Energy's performance during past extreme weather events and Nashville Electric Service's current crisis response comes down to organizational philosophy rather than merely meteorological or geographical factors. PSE treats infrastructure resilience and emergency preparedness as core business functions with dedicated budgets and executive oversight. They understand that reliable electricity isn't just a convenience--it's essential for public safety, economic stability, and community well-being.
Nashville's current suffering demonstrates the cost of inadequate preparation. Extended power outages in freezing temperatures create life-threatening conditions, particularly for vulnerable populations including the elderly and those with medical needs. The economic impact extends beyond direct utility costs to lost productivity, food spoilage, and alternative energy expenses.
As Nashville struggles to recover from this crisis, the utility industry should look to PSE's approach as a model for excellence. Their investment in technology, transparent communication, strategic workforce planning, and infrastructure hardening creates capacity for resilience in the face of increasingly frequent extreme weather events. The choice isn't between rate increases and service reliability--it's between strategic investments now and crisis costs later.
Puget Sound Energy has proven that comprehensive grid modernization and preparedness initiatives pay dividends when disaster strikes. Their track record demonstrates it's possible to maintain reliability even in the face of severe weather. Nashville's current struggles suggest there are valuable lessons to be learned from utilities that have prioritized resilience over short-term cost savings.
Not for nothing, the last time Seattle had a Republican mayor was 1969; Nashville never has had a Republican in modern history. Energy is non-partisan.

As Nashville struggles to recover from this crisis, the utility industry should look to PSE's approach as a model for excellence. Their investment in technology, transparent communication, strategic workforce planning, and infrastructure hardening creates capacity for resilience in the face of increasingly frequent extreme weather events. The choice isn't between rate increases and service reliability--it's between strategic investments now and crisis costs later. Puget Sound Energy has proven that comprehensive grid modernization and preparedness initiatives pay dividends when disaster strikes. Their track record demonstrates it's possible to maintain reliability even in the face of severe weather. Nashville's current struggles suggest there are valuable lessons to be learned from utilities that have prioritized resilience over short-term cost savings. Not for nothing, the last time Seattle had a Republican mayor was 1969; Nashville never has had a Republican in modern history. Energy is non-partisan. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: The two of us live very different lives…but we’re both fighting for this:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Warren for Senate: https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/370?source=em-header&t=1001&akid=2825%2E4032634%2EqT48HZ

You might say that Zohran Mamdani and I live two very
different lives.

Me? I’m a grandmother to three exceptional grandchildren. Zohran on the
other hand says he receives near-daily phone calls from his mother asking
when the grandchildren will arrive.

Despite this, we’re both fighting hard for every family to have the right
to childcare.

Why? Because every single person in this country — whether you’re a
grandmother, whether you’re a young millennial with eager
parents-who-want-to-be-grandparents on the phone, whether you don’t plan
to have children or don’t know yet, whether you’re a person who snarks
about “childless cat ladies” — will benefit from universal child care.

Zohran and I wrote an op-ed for USA Today laying out the case for
universal child care as an investment in our country’s economic
infrastructure. Please read it below. [ https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3555?amount=28&t=1006&akid=2825%2E4032634%2EqT48HZ ]And if you’re able, please chip
in $28 or
anything you can to power our work to get universal child care passed.

Thanks for reading — and thanks for being a part of this,

Elizabeth

USA Today
Mayor Mamdani, Sen. Warren: Everyone benefits from universal childcare

Universal childcare is the kind of investment Wall Street would tout:
Every dollar spent on early childhood care can return as much as $13. It
restores the workforce. It's basic infrastructure.

March 19, 2026

The two of us live very different lives. One of us is a grandmother to
three exceptional grandchildren. The other receives near-daily phone calls
from his mother asking when the grandchildren will arrive.

And yet, despite those differences, we share a simple conviction: Every
family in New York City ‒ and in America ‒ has a right to childcare.

In January, New York City announced a historic new investment in universal
childcare. Through a partnership struck between City Hall and New York
Gov. Kathy Hochul, free, universal childcare will soon be expanded to
every 2- and 3-year-old across the five boroughs.

Even for a city that constantly reinvents itself, this is a seismic shift.

Universal childcare can restore workforce, jump-starting the economy

It will be felt in the lives of children who grow up happier and
healthier. Kids who attend preschool are nearly 6% more likely to attend
college. It will also be felt by families who suddenly have an additional
$20,000 or more per year, per child, in their pockets.

And it will be felt when our economy is energized by parents who can stay
in their jobs, by businesses that can attract and retain top talent who
might otherwise be priced out of this city, and by an increase in economic
activity to the tune of tens of billions of dollars.

The case for universal childcare is overwhelming. It’s the kind of
investment Wall Street would tout: Every dollar spent on early childhood
care can return as much as $13. It restores the workforce. After Quebec
introduced universal childcare, women's participation in the workforce
increased by 16 percentage points.

It also addresses one of the greatest threats to our economy: families
being pushed out of the places they call home.

Childcare isn’t just care. It’s basic infrastructure, as essential to a
thriving society as roads, bridges and public transit ‒ the foundation
upon which a vibrant, flourishing society can be built.

The change New York City will soon experience is already underway in New
Mexico, which launched a groundbreaking universal childcare program in
November. But this progress shouldn’t be limited only to states that begin
with the word "new." Every family — from Alaska to Florida — deserves the
same opportunity.

If we want to protect the American dream, we begin with childcare.

Adults shouldn't have to choose between career and kids

Affordable childcare means parents are no longer forced to choose between
raising their children and keeping their jobs. It means better outcomes
for kids. And frankly, for all of us.

By committing to build childcare infrastructure, we also have an
opportunity to invest in childcare workers and to ensure that they are
paid commensurate with their training and experience.

Currently, these workers are caught in a squeeze because wages are
inadequate but parents cannot afford to pay more. The result is that 60%
of childcare centers are short-staffed.

We invest in firefighters and road maintenance crews by paying living
wages; we should make the same investments in people who care for our
babies. In fact, universal childcare may be one of the most powerful tools
we have to make life more affordable for American families.

Affordability is a key midterm elections issue

As the Democratic Party heads into the November elections, before gearing
up for a historic presidential contest in 2028, we should build our
platform around policies that are both incredibly popular across party
lines and materially improve working people’s lives.

Americans have been clear about their biggest concern: affordability.

Universal childcare answers that concern directly. For decades, the
Republican Party has championed a trickle-down economic theory that
enriches billionaires, deepens inequality, drives up inflation and leaves
working families in the dirt. It’s time for a different approach, one that
puts a dignified life within reach by investing public dollars to improve
the lives of working people.

When President Franklin D. Roosevelt enacted the New Deal, government made
people’s lives better. When President Lyndon B. Johnson pursued the Great
Society, government made people’s lives better.

When New York City delivers free, universal childcare, government will
once again make people’s lives better.

However, when the government hands out more tax cuts to millionaires and
billionaires, it improves life for only a handful of the richest people in
this country ‒ while making life harder for millions more.

We should not have to dust off history books to find examples of the
Democratic Party leading with courage and ambition. With universal
childcare, we can transform our economy, transform the lives of parents
and children, and transform how Americans see government.

We’re in the fight to get it done.

Hi Peter, Deb Haaland here.
Happy Women’s History Month. I’m thinking about my great-grandmother, my mother, and the generations of women who came before me.
My mom was born in a train boxcar where the Laguna people built a community far from home. She served in the U.S. Navy, raised four kids as a military wife, and spent more than two decades in Indian education. **I come from generations of resilient, fierce Pueblo women. They taught me to Be Fierce — to protect our communities and never back down.**
That’s why I ran for office. Standing on their shoulders, I became one of the first Native women elected to Congress and then the first Native American Cabinet secretary — and the whole time, I never stopped being fierce.
I’ve stood up to corporate polluters. I rebuilt the Department of the Interior after Trump slashed staff, cut budgets, and rolled back protections. I defended our public lands and our people when they were under attack.
And I won’t stop now.
**But I can’t do this alone.[Will you split a donation of $5 or whatever you can today between Heartland Patriots and my campaign to help me keep fighting for New Mexico?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/102027?refcode=em20260322-10207&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=5&t=2&akid=10207%2E614464%2EPe7JwC)**

Peter, right now Trump and his allies are doing everything they can to tear us down — gutting health care, raising costs, ignoring the affordability crisis, attacking reproductive freedom, dismantling voting rights, and sowing fear in our communities to hold onto power.
But I won’t back down.
I was a single mom. I relied on Medicaid, WIC, and SNAP. I worked multiple jobs and started a small salsa business to get by. I know what it means to keep fighting — even when it feels like things aren’t getting any easier.
That’s why I’m prepared to lead.
I understand affordability because I’ve lived it. I know how critical strong public schools, accessible health care, and safe communities are — because my family relied on them.
And I’ve led at the highest levels of government — in Congress and as U.S. Secretary of the Interior — where I took on tough fights and delivered real results.
Experience matters. Leadership matters. And I’m ready.
But there are Republicans ready to spend whatever it takes to bring Trump’s extreme agenda to New Mexico — and we can’t let that happen.
So I’m asking again: **[Will you chip in today to help us fight back, protect our rights, and deliver for working families, split a donation between Heartland Patriots and my campaign right now!](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/102027?refcode=em20260322-10207&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=10207%2E614464%2EPe7JwC)**

The **_Daniel Ellsberg Press Freedom and Whistleblower Protection Act_** is named in honor of the late Daniel Ellsberg, the celebrated Detroiter and whistleblower who bravely exposed government lies about the Vietnam War with the Pentagon Papers and faced charges under the _Espionage Act_.
Before he passed in 2023, Daniel expressed public support for these reforms when I introduced them as an amendment to the _National Defense Authorization Act_.
Previous Democratic and Republican presidential administrations have abused the _Espionage Act_ to undermine government transparency and target people who share critically important information with the public.
**With increasing attacks on whistleblowers, journalists, activists, and our civil liberties, we must urgently rein in the abuses of the**** _Espionage Act_****.**
If passed,**my new bill would limit the scope of the**** _Espionage Act_****** to government employees with a legal duty to protect classified information and foreign agents.**** This would prevent the use of the law against publishers, journalists, or members of the general public.
The _Daniel Ellsberg Press Freedom and Whistleblower Protection Act_ would also **increase due process standards and safeguards for whistleblowers who alert the public to wrongdoing, war crimes, and other abuses of power**.
This legislation has been endorsed by a variety of groups that advocate for our human and constitutional rights, including the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), Amnesty International USA, and the Committee to Protect Journalists.

subject: I am not going to break.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I am going to fight this with everything I have. But don’t make the mistake of thinking this is just about me. It’s about every person who has the courage to speak out against Trump.
Team: I’m writing to ask you for $5.
That’s right: just $5.
$5 because I’ve had enough of Trump and Hegseth’s attacks on our Constitution.
$5 because Donald Trump wants to stamp out any and all opposition, and he’s willing to undermine your First Amendment rights to do it.
$5 because he’s sent Pete Hegseth after me, and he’s moving ahead with a sham investigation to drag my name through the mud and destroy what I fought for during my 25 years in uniform.
I am not going to break. I am going to fight this with everything I have. But don’t make the mistake of thinking this is just about me. It’s about every person who has the courage to speak out against Trump.
Trump wants us living in fear. I don’t intend to let him win. I need your help.
**[Can you make a contribution of $5, or whatever you can afford, between my campaign and Chris Pappas to help power our work against Trump, Hegseth, and anyone else who would take away our liberties?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260322_1.M5IPt-&refcode=em20260322-1&t=1&akid=5683%2E582294%2EIRwQ9I)**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]
