Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | IRAN WAR ALERT and global markets are monitoring the situation closely. This is another unconstitutional power grab designed to silence eligible voters and rig the election in Trump’s favor. Millions of Texans could have their voices erased. The Supreme Court is taking up a case that could rip Temporary Protected
Status (TPS) away from hundreds of thousands of Syrian and Haitian
migrants — people who fled war, disaster, and instability and have built
lawful lives here for years.

And now, Trump wants to tear that all down by pushing to strip those
protections and force people back into dangerous, unstable conditions.

Lower courts have already recognized the stakes. They’ve stepped in to
block the termination of TPS while the cases move forward.

But Trump did what he always does: he ran straight to the Supreme Court,
asking it to override those rulings and clear the path for mass upheaval.

If that sounds familiar, it’s because it is.

This is the same Court that has repeatedly bent over backward for Trump —
fast-tracking decisions, bypassing full review, and handing him wins that
just happen to line up perfectly with his agenda.

If they greenlight these terminations, people will lose their status
overnight. Families uprooted, communities destabilized, and people who are
here legally will be forced back to danger because the administration says
conditions are “good enough.”

“Good enough” is not a standard for making legal decisions that shape
people’s lives. It's unacceptable.

We’re calling out this corrupt Court and demanding that decisions be made

body:
Help me unseat my corporate-backed, 30-year incumbent opponent.
#
Peter, we won.
**Last week, Denver Democrats went precinct by precinct across this city and voted in the assembly 63 to 32 to back our campaign over a 30-year incumbent!**
[](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260322-mk.iSEISh&refcode=em20260322-37593&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=37593%2E1203867%2ELA11X5)
**[Now, we have 4 days left to potentially knock our opponent off the ballot entirely. Rush a split donation now to fund our organizing efforts and ensure we’re ready for the caucuses on March 26th!](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260322-mk.iSEISh&refcode=em20260322-37593&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=37593%2E1203867%2ELA11X5)**
Diana DeGette has been in Congress since 1997, and she has decades of name recognition and a fully funded campaign sponsored by corporate PACs ready to write checks the moment she asks. But Denver Democrats – the people who show up, who organize, who actually live in this city – looked at all of that and said, “Not good enough.”
Together, we just proved that we are the most significant challenge she has faced in three decades, and we’ve done it all by running a grassroots campaign that’s not beholden to donations from Big Pharma or weapons manufacturers.
To be honest, it’s hard to even put into words what this victory means and how grateful I am to YOU for helping us get to this point.
If you know my story, you know I grew up right here in Denver watching my parents work two and three jobs just to keep us here. I’ve lived a life knowing how much groceries cost and how quickly rent has climbed for all of us. I know what it feels like to work your ass off and still wonder if you’re one bad day away from not being able to make ends meet. We’re all tired of being crushed by health insurance companies and the billionaires who buy our elected officials to increase shareholder profits.
**Denver Democrats said: ENOUGH.**
But, Peter, _winning the assembly is just the beginning._ The primary is just a couple of months away, and now that these results are public, the establishment machine is not going to give up its power quietly. They will spend and come after us.
**[I need you to show them – right now – that this movement has real fuel behind it. Can you donate whatever you can today to my campaign and Justice Democrats? Every dollar will help us unseat this corporate incumbent and win!](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260322-mk.iSEISh&refcode=em20260322-37593&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=37593%2E1203867%2ELA11X5)**
**[Contribute $5](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260322-mk.iSEISh&refcode=em20260322-37593&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=23&akid=37593%2E1203867%2ELA11X5)**
We showed up in every precinct, at every community event, in every neighborhood. That is what representation looks like, and we are just getting started.
Melat

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20260322-37593-footer&t=24&refcode2=37593_1203867_LA11X5&akid=37593%2E1203867%2ELA11X5)**

| | Peter,

My name is Katie Britt, and if it’s alright with you, I’d like to share a little about who I am. **I’m not part of the D.C. cocktail circuit, and I never will be._That’s just not who I am._**

In 2022, I was elected to represent the great state of Alabama in the United States Senate. I became the first woman in Alabama’s history to hold this seat—but that’s not why I ran.

I ran because I’m a _**mom**_ , a _**wife**_ , and a _**conservative**_ who’s fed up with the direction this country is heading. I came to Washington to fight for our families, to protect our values, and to bring some Alabama backbone to a broken system.

I didn’t come here to make friends with the political elite. I came here to stand up for the people who don’t have a voice in the room—and I’m not backing down.
---

clean_body: Everything I am started in Alabama | | | | | Peter, My name is Katie Britt, and if it’s alright with you, I’d like to share a little about who I am. I’m not part of the D.C. cocktail circuit, and I never will be.That’s just not who I am. In 2022, I was elected to represent the great state of Alabama in the United States Senate. I became the first woman in Alabama’s history to hold this seat—but that’s not why I ran. I ran because I’m a mom , a wife , and a conservative who’s fed up with the direction this country is heading. I came to Washington to fight for our families, to protect our values, and to bring some Alabama backbone to a broken system. I didn’t come here to make friends with the political elite. I came here to stand up for the people who don’t have a voice in the room—and I’m not backing down. Before coming to the Senate, I served as the first female president and CEO of the Business Council of Alabama, and before that, I was Chief of Staff to Senator Richard Shelby. I’ve never shied away from a challenge—and I’ve never forgotten who I’m fighting for. In every role I’ve held, my mission has been the same: deliver real results for Alabama families and the American people. Before starting my career in public service, I earned my undergraduate and law degrees from the University of Alabama. That experience taught me how to lead, think on my feet, and fight for what I believe in—and it laid the foundation for everything I’ve done since. But long before that, I was just a small-town girl from Enterprise, Alabama. My dad ran the local hardware store. My mom taught dance to almost every kid in town. We didn’t grow up with wealth or political connections. We came from hard work, grit, and doing things the right way.That’s how I was raised, and that’s exactly how I lead. My husband Wesley and our two amazing kids are my rock. In 2011, a tornado tore through our home and nearly took our lives. That moment changed everything, and reminded me what truly matters. Faith , family , and resilience. I’ve lived a life full of hard work, determination, and breaking barriers. There have been challenges and triumphs alike, but I wouldn’t trade any of it. My story is a testament to what America stands for—the American Dream. From a small town in Alabama, I rose to become my state’s U.S. Senator—a woman who’s breaking barriers and fighting for conservative values every day. I’m living proof of the limitless opportunity and freedom that define this country. But, I didn’t get here by playing it safe or staying quiet, and I’m not about to start now. The radical Left wants to silence conservatives like me. They want to drown out our voices and push their agenda without opposition, but I’m standing firm. I’m fighting tooth and nail to keep up and push back hard, for Alabama, for our values, and for every American who believes in freedom. The support I’ve received so far means everything, but this fight is far from over. We need the resources to keep going strong and hold our ground. Thank you, and may God bless America. Katie Britt (R-AL) | | I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong. Faith. Family. Freedom. The Left is doing everything they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored. From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul. This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Are we better off?
body:
With Greg Abbott, big promises come first, and accountability comes dead last
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
After over a decade of Greg Abbott’s leadership, I have to ask, Peter.
_**Are we better off?**_
For far too many Texans, the answer is a resounding **no**.
❌ **Public schools are closing all across the state.** Thanks to Greg Abbott’s Voucher Scam, families are worried about whether schools have the resources to support their children. Teachers are underpaid, and school districts are asked to do more with less.
❌**Texans can’t afford essential medicine.** Greg Abbott refuses to fund health care, leaving too many people without coverage and putting pressure on hospitals, clinics, and families who are already struggling with health expenses.
❌ **And Texans are _still_ living with poor infrastructure.** After several deadly infrastructure failures and repeated warnings, Texans deserve reliability and preparedness, not thoughts and prayers for the victims and their families.
With Greg Abbott, big promises come first, and accountability comes dead last.**But Texans are tired of paying the price for his poor leadership.**
Texans are tired of Greg Abbott. Tired of watching our schools, health care, and basic affordability lose priority while he plays corrupt political games just to stay in power.
That’s why I’m running for governor — because I’m determined to deliver for Texans.
Texans can’t afford another four years of Abbott, Peter. **[If you believe Texans deserve a real leader who puts everyday people ahead of special interests, will you chip in $5 today to support my campaign for governor?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260322_1_betteroff.wdNdWJ&refcode=em20260322-786&amount=5&t=1&akid=786%2E299639%2EdBe8Jl)**

Thank you,
Gina

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d4c6db60-9037-47b3-917d-d5b22691356c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Dr. Mike Goldstein is officially launching his campaign--and he's not mincing words about what's at stake.
"Washington is broken--and people here in Connecticut are paying the price," Goldstein said ahead of his March 25 kickoff in Cos Cob.
"I'm not a career politician. I'm a doctor. I solve problems--and that's exactly what I intend to do in Congress."
Goldstein is running on a message that's likely to resonate with frustrated voters: affordability, accountability, and putting people before politics.
"Families are getting crushed--by energy costs, taxes, and policies that make no sense," he said. "Meanwhile, the same politicians keep doubling down. That's not leadership--that's failure."
Framing his campaign as a direct challenge to the political status quo, Goldstein made clear this race is about more than one seat.
"This is about restoring common sense," he said. "Government should work for the people--not for itself."
And his closing message is blunt:
# _**" If you're fed up, good--you should be," Goldstein said. "Now do something about it. Join us."**_

name: Jocelyn Benson
subject: I know this work is far from over.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor

I just got back from a trip to Alabama and visited Montgomery (where I
started my career), Birmingham, and Selma.

In Montgomery, I toured the Civil Rights Memorial Center and met with a
dear friend of mine, Lecia Brooks, the Chief of Staff of the Southern
Poverty Law Center (SPLC). Many years ago, after I graduated college, I
started my career in Montgomery, Alabama working at the SPLC, where I
investigated threats to democracy and civil rights in the US and abroad.
This laid the foundation for my career and in my ongoing fight for civil
rights.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3566?t=1001&akid=1568%2E181023%2E93sNf8 ][IMG]

In Selma, I joined thousands of activists, advocates, and lawmakers in
crossing the Edmund Pettus bridge to commemorate the 61st anniversary of
Bloody Sunday. I’ve attended the annual crossing of the Edmund Pettus
Bridge in Selma since the 1990s to honor the men and women who risked
everything to secure the freedom to vote and to recommit myself to
continuing their fight.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3596?t=1002&akid=1568%2E181023%2E93sNf8 ][IMG] [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3596?t=1003&akid=1568%2E181023%2E93sNf8 ][IMG]

This trip was a reminder of the still unfinished work of the Civil Rights
Movement, and what I’ve spent my career fighting for.

I knew from a young age that I wanted to fight for justice and for our
democracy. That’s why as soon as I graduated college, I took a job at the
SPLC. And, I didn’t stop there. After law school, I moved to Detroit and
worked as a law clerk fighting to protect and defend people’s civil rights
and freedoms. And, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought every day to secure
our elections and expand voter access.

I know this work is far from over. As governor, I’ll continue the
unfinished work to build a democracy – and an economy – where all can
truly thrive and prosper. I’ll work to build more housing, take on unfair
rate hikes, expand affordable childcare, and ensure Michigan is the best
place to call home.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/3596?t=1004&akid=1568%2E181023%2E93sNf8 ]But I can’t do this work without your help. Michigan is one of the
biggest battleground races in the country this year. So, will you
contribute $10 or $25 to my campaign today to help us keep the governor’s
office blue and build a Michigan that works for everyone?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

name: David Hogg
subject: They called him a punk
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Utah has never sent a progressive to Congress. Here’s why that’s about to change.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260322-1&t=1&akid=3275%2E587540%2ElkYbn_)
Peter,
Utah Republicans cut off his mic mid-speech on the state senate floor. Multiple times.
They called him a punk.
Nate Blouin’s response?
_“If wanting a little public accountability from our state leaders makes me a punk, so be it.”_
And he kept going. That’s who Nate is — state senator, defender of Utah’s land and water, and the most consistently outspoken progressive voice in a chamber dominated by a Republican supermajority.
He’s running for Utah’s 1st Congressional District, and his primary is on June 23rd. If he wins, it’ll be history-making: **Nate would be the first progressive Democrat ever sent to Congress from Utah.**
That won’t just be a win for Utah. It’ll be a signal about where the future of the Democratic Party is headed.
**[I’ll tell you more about him and his race in a second, but first, can you split a $5 donation between Nate and Leaders We Deserve today? The earlier we have his back, the stronger his foundation to win his June primary is.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260322_1_nate.VmxECz&refcode=em20260322-3275&amount=5&t=2&akid=3275%2E587540%2ElkYbn_)**
Nate grew up with a deep love for the outdoors. The mountains, the wilderness, the water — that’s not just where he feels at peace, it’s foundational to who he is. Before he got into politics, he spent years working for clean energy companies and environmental organizations, advocating for renewable energy across the Mountain West. And In his first ever race, Nate walked into the Democratic primary and _beat a 36-year incumbent,_ winning by over 50 points.
**His very first bill as a state senator was to save the Great Salt Lake, and he’s still fighting that fight.** The lake is shrinking at an alarming rate, and as the lakebed dries up, it exposes toxic dust that gets blown directly into communities where hundreds of thousands of Utahns live. He’s introduced bill after bill to set measurable recovery goals and protect the lake’s water supply. He’s also passed a law modernizing Utah’s power grid, making it more efficient, easier to add renewable energy in the future, and reducing wildfire risk.
And Nate’s commitment to fighting for working people goes beyond policy. He’s navigated student debt, relied on SNAP benefits to get by, and lived paycheck to paycheck. **Congress needs more leaders like Nate who have actually lived that reality and know what it’s like to navigate today’s economy, not just talk about it.**
And here’s why this race matters:
Utah just went through redistricting battles that created a new seat in Salt Lake County, opening up a rare opportunity for a Democrat to flip a U.S. House seat in Utah. Voters passed a fair map initiative, Republicans tried to kill it, but a court upheld it. **Because democracy worked, there’s a real progressive running in a genuinely competitive seat.**
And just like us, Nate doesn’t take money from corporate PACs or special interests. In Congress, he’ll take on Trump, the billionaires, and the establishment — and he won’t back down.
**[His primary is June 23rd — closer than you think. Putting progressive fighters like Nate in Congress is how we build a Democratic Party that works for all of us. So Peter, can you split a $5 donation between Nate and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260322_1_nate.VmxECz&refcode=em20260322-3275&amount=5&t=3&akid=3275%2E587540%2ElkYbn_)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

He’s also passed a law modernizing Utah’s power grid, making it more efficient, easier to add renewable energy in the future, and reducing wildfire risk. And Nate’s commitment to fighting for working people goes beyond policy. He’s navigated student debt, relied on SNAP benefits to get by, and lived paycheck to paycheck. Congress needs more leaders like Nate who have actually lived that reality and know what it’s like to navigate today’s economy, not just talk about it. And here’s why this race matters: Utah just went through redistricting battles that created a new seat in Salt Lake County, opening up a rare opportunity for a Democrat to flip a U.S. House seat in Utah. Voters passed a fair map initiative, Republicans tried to kill it, but a court upheld it. Because democracy worked, there’s a real progressive running in a genuinely competitive seat. And just like us, Nate doesn’t take money from corporate PACs or special interests. In Congress, he’ll take on Trump, the billionaires, and the establishment — and he won’t back down. Thank you, David Hogg

# Cuba hit by third nationwide blackout this month
Cuba's **[power grid failed completely on March 16, 2026,](https://substack.com/redirect/bc73296b-b586-4410-86ce-c49805502885?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the third collapse in March, triggered by a generating unit failure amid aging infrastructure, fuel shortages, and U.S. blockade pressures.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bc73296b-b586-4410-86ce-c49805502885?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Cascading Failure Details:** Outage began at Nuevitas plant in Camaguey province, causing chain reaction; micro-islands activated for hospitals and vital services.
**Frequent Disruptions Worsen:** Daily blackouts up to 12 hours from fuel shortages compound breakdowns, disrupting work, food storage, and even hospital surgeries.
**Fuel Supply Crisis Deepens:** No oil imports for three months, with Cuba producing only 40% needed; Venezuela shipments halted and U.S. tariffs threaten suppliers.
**Government Blames Blockade:** President Diaz-Canel cites U.S. energy restrictions and Trump demands for prisoner release and liberalization as key factors.

# AI agents threaten white-collar jobs in massive scale shift
AI deployment is **[sparking dread for U.S. workers](https://substack.com/redirect/cf026a46-b972-4021-899b-2a5a839306ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as leaders describe agents replacing huge swaths of human tasks, with early signs in layoffs at major firms and a 4% net job reduction in vulnerable sectors.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cf026a46-b972-4021-899b-2a5a839306ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Job Market Dread Grows:** Executives now see AI eliminating roles rapidly, especially white-collar work, leaving average or older workers facing long unemployment or lower-tier shifts like ridesharing.
**Early-Career Roles Hit Hardest:** Surveys show companies in AI-impacted sectors cut 4% net jobs, with the highest unreplaced eliminations among those with no prior experience.
**Wall Street Pressure Mounts:** By 2027 scrutiny on operating expenses will intensify to identify AI optimizers, accelerating near-term labor market impacts per Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire.
**Productivity Superpowers Emerge:** Embracing agentic AI grants dramatic impact gains for adapters, while non-adopters face replacement on massive scale in white-collar fields.

# OpenAI scales back data center ambitions ahead of IPO
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has shifted **[from aggressive multibillion-dollar infrastructure deals to a more measured approach,](https://substack.com/redirect/2b9a43b3-7f90-4b66-81d4-78b8e5cc700d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** citing construction challenges and Wall Street demands for fiscal responsibility before a potential 2026 IPO.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b9a43b3-7f90-4b66-81d4-78b8e5cc700d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Compute Constraints Force Pivot:** After $1.4 trillion commitment talks and deals like $100 billion Nvidia pact, OpenAI now targets $600 billion compute spend by 2030 tied to revenue.
**Stargate Project Hits Reality:** Flagship Abilene Texas site with Oracle and SoftBank faced weather disruptions and supply chain issues, leading to reliance on cloud partners over ownership.
**Market Demands Discipline:** Analysts note OpenAI retreating from reckless growth to justify spending, emphasizing enterprise focus and high-productivity use cases amid competition.
**IPO Pressures Temper Spending:** Valued at $730 billion recently, the company shelves ambitious builds for partner-leased capacity to appeal to public market investors.
* * *

# "Low Earth Orbit" satellites draw $45B investment surge in 2025
Low Earth Orbit **[emerges as critical infrastructure](https://substack.com/redirect/93edf25b-d3c8-4647-b482-d868704abdd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with $45 billion invested in 2025, driven by constellations from SpaceX, Amazon, and Nvidia pushing connectivity, AI computing, and global coverage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/93edf25b-d3c8-4647-b482-d868704abdd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Massive Constellation Expansions:** SpaceX's Starlink exceeds 9,500 satellites with plans for millions, while Amazon targets over 3,000 and Blue Origin aims for 5,000 by 2027.
**Orbital Computing Frontier:** Nvidia unveils platform for space-based AI data centers and autonomous operations, calling space computing the "final frontier" at GTC 2026.
**Strategic Asset Recognition:** LEO delivers faster speeds, lower costs, and broad coverage, likened to earthly ports or grids with over $400 billion in space economy investment since 2009.
**Governance Challenges Rise:** Experts warn current regulations lag commercial scale, risking debris and interference as U.S., China, and Europe pour billions into networks.

# Wealthy shift to jewelry as safe-haven asset
Amid market volatility and uncertainty,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/3cd48e63-b5ed-49db-a184-fce66ecf16a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[high-net-worth buyers flock to fine jewelry](https://substack.com/redirect/3cd48e63-b5ed-49db-a184-fce66ecf16a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --especially colored gemstones--as a tangible store of value with strong resale performance.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3cd48e63-b5ed-49db-a184-fce66ecf16a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Record Auction Sales Signal Demand:** Tiffany Paraiba tourmaline necklace fetched $4.2 million at Christie's, 10 times low estimate, highlighting appetite for exceptional pieces.
**Gold Prices Boost Appeal:** Soaring gold above $4,500 an ounce reinforces jewelry's investment status, outperforming soft luxury like handbags in resale durability.
**Colored Gems Surge in Popularity:** Rubies, sapphires, and emeralds draw collectors seeking unique alternatives to diamonds, with auction premiums 2-3 times estimates.
**Defensive Hard Asset Trend:** Experts note tangible assets retain value in inflation and tension, with branded pieces showing mid-single-digit annual increases long-term.

clean_body: I don’t trust what I’m seeing | Fellow American, When it comes to polling, there’s certain organizations you simply can’t trust. I know that better than anyone... That’s why it’s so vital that we conduct our own polling, especially when there’s a discrepancy with the numbers like what we’re seeing right now. On one hand, polling shows voters prefer Republicans over Democrats on nearly every key issue: National Security: Immigration: Foreign policy: Trade: National debt: But at the same time, polling by the mainstream media shows Democrats have surged out to a whopping on the generic ballot for the midterms. We won three AP national championships, and I coached future Hall-of-Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. I spent a short stint as the head coach for Ole Miss before becoming the head coach for the Auburn Tigers in 1998. I solidified my career there, making eight consecutive bowl appearances, winning five SEC Western Division Titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004 when I was named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year, among other awards. I continued coaching at Texas Tech University and the University of Cincinnati until I retired from coaching in 2016 as one of the top 50 most-winning college football coaches of all time. But I wasn't done winning just yet. In 2020, I went from Coach Tuberville to Senator Tuberville. After talking to my fellow Alabamians, I was enlightened by President Trump's concerns about the direction of our country, and I decided to do something about it. I ran for the United States Senate and won. Throughout my time in Washington, D.C., I 've fought nonstop on President Trump's behalf. Whether it was fighting back against the countless witch-hunts, challenging the Biden-Harris Administration's Radical and harmful policies, or working with President Trump to secure our border, protect women in sports, and make our military prioritize readiness over wokeness, I always worked hard. I stood on principle, just like my folks taught me at a young age. Now, I 'm running for Governor in Alabama so I can continue making an impact for my community back home. The Radical Left has circled me as one of their top gubernatorial targets to defeat in 2026. They're going to spend MILLIONS of dollars trying to beat me. But if coaching in the SEC has taught me one thing, it's this: there will always be a rival trying to bring you down, but with hard work and a strong team, you can go 13-0. I 'm looking to go 2-0 in my lifetime as a political candidate, and I need your help to do so. I won't take up more of your time. Best, Coach Tommy Tuberville | Meet Coach Tuberville: Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces. In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud. In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others. In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? name: John Padora For Colorado
subject: This campaign ends - but the movement we built together will last a lifetime.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Padora for Colorado
body:
After 16,000 miles, 14 counties, and a year of grassroots organizing, our campaign comes to an end - but the friendships, the movement, and the fight
| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/aTLV2iH9KsGcRqt4Y-NoIA~~/AAUS1hA~/01JlWy5ADNBabOZcPokUwhsvjLBV8cJEqwe69aLAhNyOO2kFR5uqqVHEwxazZVpaSmS8fzDyVO9i0x4ffBGxAJBGOYYiVQmBJORCi7wUIpWP8YMObhlHAkSqMfJUL7Wd)
| | ******Friend,** **It is with a heavy heart that I share this with you today.** Last weekend, after the results of the Douglas County Assembly, our path to ballot access effectively closed. My opponent, Eileen Laubacher, received 100 percent of the delegates in Douglas County and now carries a supermajority heading into the Congressional District Assembly. Under Colorado law, candidates can reach the ballot either by earning 30 percent of the delegate vote through the caucus and assembly process or by gathering nearly 3,000 petition signatures. Our campaign chose the caucus and assembly route because we believed in engaging grassroots Democrats across the district and earning support through that process. Our team was ready to pivot. We were prepared to mobilize, to organize, and to secure the thousands of petition signatures required in just a matter of days. **But I made the decision that I could not ask that of you.** Too many of you have already sacrificed your time, your money, and your energy to build this campaign. I could not in good conscience ask you to give even more when our path to ballot access had narrowed so dramatically. **And so today, I am terminating my campaign for Congress.** While this is not the result we hoped for, I accept it as part of the democratic process. Campaigns test our ideas, our resilience, and our commitment to what we believe in. Sometimes the journey continues forward - and sometimes it ends here. In this case, I believe big money spoke louder than policy issues, communication, and true grassroots engagement. That is the unfortunate reality of our political system today. But despite my disagreement, I respect the outcome and the process that brought us here. Still, I would be lying if I said this doesn’t hurt. What saddens me most is that roughly 1.5 percent of Democratic voters in CD4 effectively decided that there would be no primary election - no broader choice for voters, no choice for progressives, and no voice for generations who are often unable to participate in these processes and are too often left unheard. At the Douglas County Assembly, I warned delegates about this exact risk. When voters feel like the outcome has been decided before they ever have a chance to participate, it breeds apathy, frustration, and distrust. I urged delegates to allow a primary election - a robust exchange of ideas - a race to the top where different visions could compete openly so that whoever emerged would be sharper, stronger, and fully prepared to defeat Lauren Boebert in November. But the delegates made their choice. I sincerely wish Eileen the best as she takes on Lauren Boebert. I truly hope she carries forward the values that so many of you brought into this campaign. Healthcare is a fundamental human right.
Working families deserve universal childcare.
Housing must become affordable again.
Taxes should be lower for working people and higher for the wealthiest one percent.
We must stop endless wars and reinvest in peace and humanitarian leadership.
Immigration reform requires judges and due process - not militarized enforcement. Over the last twelve months, together, we pushed this conversation further toward the progressive vision that so many working families believe in. **And what we accomplished together should never be forgotten.** Since launching this campaign in April of 2025: • We drove more than 16,000 miles across this district in our family vehicles
• We visited 14 counties across Colorado’s Fourth District
• We held 7 town halls across 4 counties
• We walked in parades in Castle Rock, Highlands Ranch, and Loveland
• We hosted countless house parties and community meet and greets
• We attended numerous candidate forums and public events in our communities But more than anything else - **we built something real.** A working class coalition of men, women, and people across the full spectrum of identities - including LGBTQ Coloradans and trans and non-binary members of our community - who came together from different backgrounds, cultures, religions, generations, and walks of life because they believed in what we were building. People from urban communities and rural towns.
People from different religions, cultures, and traditions.
People who identify as Democrats and independents.
People who had never participated in politics before. People from across the political spectrum who believed our country could do better. People came together not because of money or power - but because they believed in the possibility of change. And I will never forget something that happened at the assembly this weekend. Two voters came up to me and told me they had been registered as unaffiliated voters for nearly forty years. They said this campaign inspired them to finally register as Democrats so they could be part of the process - because they believed in this vision. **Hearing that humbled me beyond words.** Moments like that remind me this campaign was always about something bigger than one election. **It was the honor of a lifetime to fight for you.** It was the honor of a lifetime to stand alongside you, to organize with you, and to work to carry your voices to Washington. **And I am deeply sorry that I will not be able to fulfill that responsibility.** What I will carry with me from this journey are the people. You made phone calls, wrote postcards, and called delegates.
You donated what you could - 5 dollars, 50 dollars, 500 dollars.
You drove across counties.
You gave evenings and weekends away from your families because you believed in what we were building. **This campaign only existed because of you.** And to so many of you, what began as a campaign became something much deeper. We forged friendships that will last a lifetime. Many of you are no longer just supporters - **you are friends and you are family.** We met in so many ways - protesting on street corners, organizing at the Capitol in Denver, advocating for change inside the party system, traveling across the plains, gathering at town halls, and building community across this district. Those bonds will stay with me forever. A special thank you to my incredible wife Amber, who sacrificed more than anyone to make this campaign possible. And to my three amazing children - who gave up time with their parents so that we could try to serve our community - I love you more than words can express. To my team - you know who you are. There are too many of you to name, but you inspired me every single day. You motivated me when I felt like quitting.
You made me laugh when things felt impossible.
You lifted me up when things felt heavy. **I will forever be grateful that our paths crossed.** As for me, this marks the end of my time in electoral politics. But **the fight does not end - it simply changes shape.** I started this journey as an activist and organizer, and that is where I will return. There are victories to be achieved beyond the ballot box. I will continue to fight for healthcare, housing, peace, working families, and a future worth handing to our children and grandchildren. When things feel dark - when the division, the fear, and the chaos feel overwhelming - remember this: **You are not alone.** Before closing, one final note - because the campaign is ending, any recurring donations will be automatically canceled as quickly as possible so no additional contributions are processed moving forward. To every supporter who contributed financially - thank you. Your generosity helped build this grassroots movement. If you ever need me, you know where to reach me. My phone number remains the same: 970-834-3124 **Our campaign may end today.** **But the movement we built, the friendships we formed, and the fight for a better future will continue.** With gratitude and solidarity, **John Padora**
Working Dad • Fighter • Engineer
Candidate for Congress in CO 04 ****

subject: Tell them your vote is not for sale

body:
| | | Peter, Billionaires and AIPAC have been buying our elections for so long that most people stopped believing it could be any other way. This week, Illinois proved them wrong. AIPAC and its allies poured over $21 million into four Illinois primaries. In the biggest race, their candidate finished third. The candidate who beat them said it best: "this district is not for sale." They're already spinning it as a victory because the most progressive candidates didn't win. name: Tim Kaine
subject: Why I’m supporting a YES vote on Virginia’s redistricting amendment:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Virginians for Fair Elections
body:
Virginia voters have the opportunity to make sure our elections stay in the hands of the people, not politicians.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260322-364&t=1&akid=364%2E12592%2Eofk7aq)
Friends,
Donald Trump has made it clear that he’s willing to bend, break, or bulldoze democratic norms if it helps him cling to power.
Now, with the midterm elections coming up, Virginia voters have the opportunity to make sure elections stay in the hands of the people, not politicians.
**_Critically, the upcoming referendum gives _voters_ the right to decide what comes next._**
I’m supporting a YES vote on Virginia’s redistricting amendment because I believe this will restore fairness in our elections and prevent Donald Trump from locking in power months before November.
[**If you’re on board, I’m asking you to join me in supporting Virginians for Fair Elections. They’re working around the clock to reach voters across the Commonwealth with clear, factual information about what this amendment does and why it matters. Will you contribute whatever amount is meaningful to you today?**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260322_2.oMVfel&amount=3&refcode=20260322-364&t=2&akid=364%2E12592%2Eofk7aq)
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260322_2.oMVfel&amount=3&refcode=20260322-364&t=21&akid=364%2E12592%2Eofk7aq)**
This election is happening on April 21, not in November.
**That means time is running out for the ballot measure committee to reach voters with important education and information.**
The stakes are incredibly high in 2026, and Virginia voters have a serious responsibility in front of us to consider this redistricting amendment and make our choice about what happens next. Unlike other states around the country pushing redistricting, this decision will be made directly by the people of our Commonwealth.
[************If you’re with me on this** , I hope you’ll consider donating to support Virginians for Fair Elections today. I believe this amendment will safeguard Virginia’s elections ahead of this year’s crucial midterm elections. **](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260322_2.oMVfel&amount=3&refcode=20260322-364&t=22&akid=364%2E12592%2Eofk7aq)
Thank you for standing up for our democracy.
Tim Kaine
U.S. Senator for Virginia

Peter, we just hit
a major milestone! Our campaign has surpassed over 300 public events
across Michigan.

[ A ]A group photo of Abdul with supporters in a coffee shop

We’re filling up union halls and coffee shops because Michiganders are
tired of politicians who show up at election time, read from a script, and
disappear.

[ A ]A photo from a Small Businesses for Abdul event

They want someone who actually listens and will use every tool at their
disposal to bring about positive, lasting change. That's Abdul.

[ A ]A photo of the crowd at a Women for Abdul event

At every single one of these events, Abdul does what he's always done: he
explains why things are broken and exactly what we're going to do about
it.

[ Another ]Another group photo of Abdul with more supporters

But we’ll be honest, putting this many events on the calendar is
incredibly expensive. We have to budget for staff, travel, venue
logistics, printed materials, and more.

Every event we host across this massive state costs real money — money
that, unlike our opponents, we can't raise from corporate PACs or
billionaire donors.

We depend on folks like you,
Peter. Every dollar you give
helps us keep Abdul on the road, meeting Michiganders in every corner of
this state.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260322em-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260322em-rs]
President Trump just issued a stunning ultimatum.
He said he won’t sign any legislation at all unless Congress passes his voter bill — the so-called SAVE America Act.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260322em-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260322em-rs]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260322em-rs]
You read that right: The President of the United States is threatening to hold the entire federal government hostage in order to force through a sweeping overhaul of election laws that could strip away the right to vote from over 20 million Americans... right before a major election.
That bill would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, beyond what is already required, and impose strict new voter ID requirements nationwide. In fact, whenever somebody updates their address or changes their political party they would need to show their passport or birth certificate.
And most concerningly for Oregonians, the SAVE Act bans vote-by-mail elections.
Supporters claim it’s about “election integrity.” But here’s the truth: voting fraud in the United States is extraordinarily rare, and millions of eligible voters don’t have immediate access to the documents this law would require.
This isn’t about security — it’s about power. And when politicians can’t win the argument with voters, they start trying to change who gets to vote in the first place.
In Oregon we’ve built one of the most secure and accessible election systems in the country. We’ve expanded access while protecting integrity. We’ve shown that you can make voting easier and keep elections safe.
We should be defending that model — not tearing it down.
That’s why I’m fighting back against Donald Trump’s illegal power grab and working overtime to defend our democracy from his attacks. But I can’t do it alone.
So I’m asking you personally to join me in this fight by chipping in $10, $25, or more right now. Can I count on you to step up and take a stand for our democracy in the face of Donald Trump’s lies? And I’m asking you to make your voice heard. We can’t take anything for granted. The future of our democracy is at stake. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260322em-rs]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260322em-rs]
Thank you,
Tobias Read

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Dr. Martin Weiss, who has called major financial events long before others, now warns of a $112 trillion crisis hiding in America's "basement." subject: From ribbon cuttings to Waffle House

body:
Just another day as mayor of Columbia

| | | | |
---
Hey y’all, Every now and then, you have a day that reminds you why you love where you live. Earlier this month, I had one of those days here in Columbia. I rode my bike over from the law office to a small business ribbon-cutting and spent some time catching up with neighbors and friends. After that, I stopped by the local bike shop for a quick tune-up, popped into the bookstore downtown to pick up something new to read, and later had the chance to read poetry with a group of fourth graders at Woodard Elementary’s “Spring Into Reading.” [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/1eVB7FJepGlxihgK9QJekg~~/AAUS1hA~/gi3J9DNzjln6efpHHSo0_B7hoHB2LHE85sbHZH14a6oFR_MRtpzFoTPzsg92b4gBc1hlV59ddI5JprgnR5ga9iZdE6y3920aM-iefaWIahR56_rFCR7NhzHaFGoOJCd1v7d8uBMUKU__Z52pMhh5zNHS_qv2aMmdNp9XjjfUqvTSvaZSojYhLm3LZ8cdKUMLehXcs7J11TXSO4VF7ql8EuhCTf4C_yTOSJi_oXkMc1GrKt-YLGpqYAD33sg_tB24) The day wrapped up the way a lot of good days in small towns do — dinner at Waffle House. Days like that remind me what public service is really about. It’s not cable news debates or political theater. It’s being part of a community and working to make it a little stronger every day. Sometimes I think Washington could benefit from a little more of that mindset — maybe even a reminder to step outside and “touch grass.” That’s the perspective I’ll bring with me to Congress: the steady, practical approach you learn from serving a hometown like Columbia. clean_body: Just another day as mayor of Columbia | | | | | Hey y’all, Every now and then, you have a day that reminds you why you love where you live. Earlier this month, I had one of those days here in Columbia. I rode my bike over from the law office to a small business ribbon-cutting and spent some time catching up with neighbors and friends. After that, I stopped by the local bike shop for a quick tune-up, popped into the bookstore downtown to pick up something new to read, and later had the chance to read poetry with a group of fourth graders at Woodard Elementary’s “Spring Into Reading.” The day wrapped up the way a lot of good days in small towns do — dinner at Waffle House. Days like that remind me what public service is really about. It’s not cable news debates or political theater. It’s being part of a community and working to make it a little stronger every day. Sometimes I think Washington could benefit from a little more of that mindset — maybe even a reminder to step outside and “touch grass.” That’s the perspective I’ll bring with me to Congress: the steady, practical approach you learn from serving a hometown like Columbia. ~~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately: | | ~ | ~ | ~ | ~ | Grateful you’re part of this team. — Chaz | | ---|---|--- About Chaz Molder Chaz Molder is the Mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, serving since 2019 and re-elected in 2022. But today, we’re highlighting just three you need to know: ENDORSED ✔️ Myrna Muñoz – Oregon’s 15th State Senate District = JanePAC is proud to announce we’re endorsing Myrna Muñoz! A labor organizer, bilingual educator, and fearless climate champion, Myrna Muñoz is challenging incumbent Sen. Janeen Sollman, D-Hillsboro for Oregon Senate District 15. While Sollman has supported and even sponsored incentives for data centers, Myrna has publicly stood with her community, fighting for their right to have a say in whether these projects move forward and damage their land, air, water, and quality of life. = = ENDORSED ✔️ Randy Villegas – U.S. Congress, CA-22 = Randy Villegas is running in one of the most competitive congressional races in the country in California’s 22nd District. As someone who grew up in the Central Valley, Randy knows exactly what these communities are facing: extreme heat, water insecurity, and politicians who too often side with corporations over people. Even though the Central Valley helps feed the entire country, it remains one of the most polluted places in America. Randy is running to hold corporations to account, including some of the same corporations that have helped bankroll his opponent, Jasmeet Bains. = = ENDORSED ✔️ Peggy Flanagan – U.S. Senate, MN = Peggy Flanagan is exactly the kind of leader JanePAC is proud to support for U.S. Senate in Minnesota! As Lieutenant Governor, she helped make Minnesota one of the first states to require 100% carbon-free energy by 2040. She secured over $1 billion for climate resilience and clean energy. She publicly opposed the Line 3 pipeline. And she's rejected fossil fuel money her entire career. But this race won’t be an easy one to win. Peggy’s opponent, Angie Craig, has taken donations from the energy industry. A Chevron-funded PAC has even spent over half a million dollars (so far) on digital ads to boost Craig’s campaign. Compare that with Peggy, who’s proven she can’t be bought by Big Oil, and the stakes are clear: we need to win this one. = = Thanks for your support — together, we can elect climate leaders who will fight for the planet and the futures we deserve. – Team JanePAC | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. The VA is under siege every single day. Seems like every week there’s another attempt to slash care, staff, or disability ratings. This isn’t normal, and Vets are suffering.
#
Peter, it’s not easy to be a Veteran right now.
Trump’s made sure of that.
The VA is under siege every single day. Seems like every week there’s another attempt to slash care, staff, or disability ratings. This isn’t normal, and Vets are suffering.
We’ve had to watch as good, principled leaders are forced out — generals, admirals, senior officers, even down to NCOs and enlisted who have spent years in service only to be fired or forced out because they aren’t viewed as sufficiently loyal or supplicant to Trump. That goes for career staff with decades of experience at the State Department, USAID, even intelligence and law enforcement agencies, too.
And now, we’re seeing the same exact mistakes that got us deployed to combat in the last forever wars being repeated with Iran. We’re fighting an illegal war, the GOP is doing nothing to stop it, it’s being led by absolute idiots, and American kids are footing the bill.
Seeing all of that, it’s not easy.
What is getting us through is this team, and this work. We’ve built the largest Veterans organization on the left over the last 20 years, and we are firing on all cylinders right now. We’re grateful to have a place at VoteVets, and we hope you feel the same.
[**And if our work means anything to you, or has any value, we’re asking you to make a donation and support us. The donation itself is what’s most important here. Proud to be a Take BAC Congress candidate! | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSrn4JnyYtk1EREaCYHldIw2Es-lCsKe-k7RYeRErCjUmpL6YWg0aqprxBCSlqaUKjL6uf8EDq6vQVEaFZEFWaTvOKtPnFc2PEalY2SnM4_7VESUZcYSpegKWfgkimG-zW1Uv2MpxP4hJGK0P7LA2s2G9S7GmE-bUoqohxmDytsER7vjbG_Zixj7aQPx6HvK3KzzR_j-VHXM21JFBXXLYSy/4p5/MQdv28JASnm9vROrXzsF3A/h0/h001.L3h469zvCLAD3Fgj_HeCrkpQkARC2q3y-UbzxVx8LXA)

Peter, There is something that happens when you stand on the steps of the United States Capitol. You feel the weight of it. You think about every vote that expanded who this democracy belonged to and the generations that fought to be included in the promise of that building. I stood there this week in the cold with a group of Democratic candidates from across the country and I felt every bit of that weight and I was proud to carry it.

As a charter member of **Take BAC Congress** , I was honored to stand with my fellow Democratic candidates and to deliver the closing speech at their pledge event on those steps. The pledge is exactly the kind of thing our founders would have demanded of the people they entrusted with this republic. Term limits so that public service stays _service_ and stops becoming a career. A ban on members of Congress trading stocks on information the rest of us do not have access to. Getting corporate money out of politics so that votes reflect constituents and not donors. A cooling off period before members can cash in on their time in office by becoming lobbyists. And holding the Supreme Court to the same ethics standards we expect of every other institution in this democracy. All of it is overdue. [**Help us get to Congress and fight for every one of these reforms from inside the building where they matter most.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt82acdbCpFgR5yfueLo7NqBKX3tX5zwo5bxhQjuMLMN9Ranw8PTu7P8ua9FsxUika_6lbkT24mCXg0d1xtUdfBZcuYxZtIdhrjIJ2tT1mxAgdu_WRJwarETCngxmsBp5tD6-dtg1_xr5qihSyPYAAoGORCiA4JSiUqKTpvZVbIB6VCu0_SqGOVXAgY5I3jvuyBQrGCkjmYJC4WWQTA4oJdl3ZhHxfPbUfJ824Yt0QlZlk8q9cMqgtFGsLBmQMkRJqqxcjUJx4dMwZcwA0DvzBNKY/4p5/MQdv28JASnm9vROrXzsF3A/h3/h001.c6y-s4P0UiwYU_8JBlUUI4dEvf_T8dZhIa_P1rlTj9s) Keith Self has been in that building for years and has done nothing to advance a single one of them. He trades the access and the influence of his office for the donor relationships that keep him there and votes the way his corporate backers need him to vote. **He is exactly the kind of career politician these reforms are designed to remove.** Standing on those steps I thought about what Service Before Self actually means in practice. It means you do not go to Washington to get rich. You do not go to build a lobbying career on the back of your committee assignments. You do not go to trade stocks on insider knowledge while your constituents are trying to make rent. You go because the republic your founders built in that building deserves someone willing to protect it. [**Help us get there. Every dollar you put behind this campaign right now is a vote for the kind of Congress those steps were built to house.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt82acdbCpFgR5yfueLo7NqBKX3tX5zwo5bxhQjuMLMN9RX5A-gsdJU62bE-tYgNZ-XRNC84HCye0KkdTsNarvTSpYaecGp3b_LYMqHnjnBqKHABvGXWnfwwYlooIyS7h8GjdilPUSdX76neexl2v1TC6BtAyR6ryoKlI-jI_G3-EzV7vcI77UupUb-TE7Lyb8cWVAw847aokDnXzXztV0Vx7ZLPknPZ0wz_9dvlHkgywqey-9Usk5sib54F_bxqUaXBX3ExYxzbs6kGOdpVqFzGI/4p5/MQdv28JASnm9vROrXzsF3A/h4/h001.KUzUOkYkfWy-V6FdJydWPPOEKOq6QgZ8OlfX7SY-Fzk) Very respectfully, Evan Hunt Candidate for U.S. Congress TX-03

clean_body: Proud to be a Take BAC Congress candidate! | | Peter, There is something that happens when you stand on the steps of the United States Capitol. You feel the weight of it. You think about every vote that expanded who this democracy belonged to and the generations that fought to be included in the promise of that building. I stood there this week in the cold with a group of Democratic candidates from across the country and I felt every bit of that weight and I was proud to carry it. | As a charter member of Take BAC Congress , I was honored to stand with my fellow Democratic candidates and to deliver the closing speech at their pledge event on those steps. The pledge is exactly the kind of thing our founders would have demanded of the people they entrusted with this republic. Term limits so that public service stays service and stops becoming a career. A ban on members of Congress trading stocks on information the rest of us do not have access to. Getting corporate money out of politics so that votes reflect constituents and not donors. A cooling off period before members can cash in on their time in office by becoming lobbyists. And holding the Supreme Court to the same ethics standards we expect of every other institution in this democracy. All of it is overdue. Keith Self has been in that building for years and has done nothing to advance a single one of them. He trades the access and the influence of his office for the donor relationships that keep him there and votes the way his corporate backers need him to vote. He is exactly the kind of career politician these reforms are designed to remove. Standing on those steps I thought about what Service Before Self actually means in practice.
